text:
Kevin Fiala made his season debut on Nov. 12 against the Islanders, nine months after a frightening injury at the Olympics, and four games in, the story is simply that he's back. His wife's reaction to the debut got its own headlines. The Kings, shorthanded up front, need what he brings.

Four games is far too few to judge. He has one assist, four shots and 16.9 minutes a night, and Los Angeles has been outchanced with him at five on five. That's what a long layoff looks like. The NHL.com insider piece this week said he and Mats Zuccarello are making strides in their returns.

What he was is the guide. He's a finisher by trade, with 229 goals before this season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 89th percentile among forwards for chances from the slot. Evolving-Hockey had his expected wins last season (1.1) well above his actual ones, so the chances were there even then. Watch whether he starts getting to that slot again; the goals follow the looks.
headline: Fiala returns nine months after the Olympics
